output.brief: Store 14's rise may not be real. The Q1–Q3 figures are estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error band of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across chain history, about half of stores showing two straight rises like this were not confirmed by the year-end count. Store 14's past full counts ran 1.5–1.8%. The rise is 0.8 points, so it is only slightly beyond that band. Shoplifting logs rose chain-wide after the incident app launched on 1 April, so the store's log growth says little. Neighbouring stores without self-checkout did not rise. That doesn't clear self-checkout, but it doesn't convict it either. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and showed bale runs, not theft. Sales mix did not change. Recommendation: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and decline Regional Operations' proposal to drop it. Dropping it would remove the only reliable measurement. Hold off on pulling or staffing the self-checkout lanes, hiring a guard, or disciplining the stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Doubling cycle counts adds little. I am moderately sure of this. The causes remain open until the count.
